question: What does the idiom 'To beat a dead horse' mean?

options.text: Waste time on a hopeless issue

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. 'Waste time on a hopeless issue'. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"To beat a dead horse"** means to waste time or energy on a topic or issue that has already been resolved or is hopeless. (बेकार के मुद्दे पर समय बर्बाद करना) • **Example:** Trying to convince him to change his mind about the decision is like beating a dead horse. • It implies that further discussion or effort on the matter will yield no positive results and is therefore pointless. (यह बताता है कि आगे चर्चा या प्रयास का कोई परिणाम नहीं होगा और यह व्यर्थ है।) Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: Be overconfident** (अतिआत्मविश्वासी होना): Being excessively self-assured or arrogant about one's abilities. • **Example:** His overconfidence in the competition led to his downfall. • **Option 2: Win a competition** (प्रतियोगिता जीतना): To achieve victory in a contest or challenge. • **Example:** She trained hard and managed to win the competition. • **Option 3: Encourage others** (दूसरों को प्रोत्साहित करना): To motivate or inspire others to take action or feel confident. • **Example:** The teacher encouraged the students to participate in the event. 6f:Tc97, The correct answer is: **Captivity**.
